description: Create the core typing engine module (src/typing/) with: ResponseBuffer (immutable response storage), TypingQueue (position tracking, pause/resume state machine), InjectionScheduler (timing/humanization control), and AbortController. This is the backbone that all other features build on.
steps: Create src/typing/ResponseBuffer.js - An immutable buffer class that stores AI response text snapshots. Methods: create(text) returns frozen buffer with id/text/timestamp, getPosition(), getRemaining(). This prevents race conditions from streaming updates.

Create src/typing/TypingQueue.js - State machine managing typing position. States: idle, typing, paused, aborted. Properties: buffer reference, currentPosition (character index), Methods: load(buffer), advance(count), pause(), resume(), abort(), reset(), getState(), getProgress(). Emits events via EventEmitter pattern (Node.js events module in main process).

Create src/typing/HumanizationEngine.js - Computes delays between keystrokes. Config: baseWPM, burstSize, punctuationDelay, sentenceDelay, jitterRange, startupDelay. Methods: getNextDelay(char, context), setSpeed(wpm), getConfig(), updateConfig(patch). Uses randomization for natural feel.

Create src/typing/InjectionScheduler.js - Orchestrates the typing loop. Takes a queue + humanization engine + backend. Methods: start(), stop(), pause(), resume(), skipSentence(), setSpeed(wpm). Internally runs a recursive setTimeout loop that: checks queue state, gets next char(s), computes delay via humanization, calls backend.inject(). Handles granularity modes: character, word, sentence, paragraph.
Create src/typing/AbortController.js - Simple abort mechanism. Methods: abort(), isAborted(), reset(), onAbort(callback). Used by scheduler to immediately stop injection.
Create src/typing/index.js - CommonJS barrel export of all typing modules.
Ensure all modules use CommonJS (require/module.exports) since they run in Electron main process.
acceptance_criteria: All files in src/typing/ pass `node --check` syntax validation
ResponseBuffer.create() returns a frozen object with text, id, timestamp
TypingQueue correctly transitions between idle/typing/paused/aborted states
HumanizationEngine produces variable delays based on character context
InjectionScheduler can be instantiated with mock backend and drives injection loop
AbortController signals abort to registered callbacks
verification: Run `node --check src/typing/ResponseBuffer.js src/typing/TypingQueue.js src/typing/HumanizationEngine.js src/typing/InjectionScheduler.js src/typing/AbortController.js src/typing/index.js`
Run `node -e "const typing = require('./src/typing'); console.log(Object.keys(typing));"` to confirm exports

Run `node -e "const {ResponseBuffer} = require('./src/typing'); const b = ResponseBuffer.create('hello'); console.assert(b.text === 'hello'); console.assert(Object.isFrozen(b)); console.log('ResponseBuffer OK');"`
Run `node -e "const {TypingQueue} = require('./src/typing'); const q = new TypingQueue(); console.assert(q.getState() === 'idle'); console.log('TypingQueue OK');"`

Run `node -e "const {HumanizationEngine} = require('./src/typing'); const h = new HumanizationEngine({baseWPM: 60}); const d = h.getNextDelay('a', {}); console.assert(d > 0); console.log('HumanizationEngine OK');"`
findings: All 6 modules created and verified. node --check passes, require() barrel export works, all functional tests pass (state machine transitions, frozen buffers, injection loop completion, abort callbacks). Prettier reports all files unchanged (already formatted correctly). HumanizationEngine startup delay is 500ms by default. InjectionScheduler tested with high WPM and 1ms startup for fast completion.
